magic_signatures.ascii: DISNEY SNOWBOARD (logical order; raw .sav stores each 8-byte block reversed: block0 raw 532059454e534944 = 'S YENSID', block1 raw 44452414f42574f4e = 'DRAOBWON' byte-order reversed)

checksums.name: no_verified_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: No checksum verified. Tested sum8, sum16 (byte sum), sum of u16_le words, xor8, xor16, CRC16-MODBUS, CRC16-ARC, CRC16-CCITT (inits 0xFFFF/0x0000/0x1D0F) and CRC32 over header/record/table ranges in raw and per-block-reversed (logical) views of both saves (e.g. sum16 logical 0x20-0x58=0x1328, 0x60-0x98=0x14AF, 0xA0-0x140=0x3A8B vs candidate 0x03F7: all mismatch), plus a block-aligned brute force (2080 ranges x 5 algorithms x 4 views = 41600 tests) whose single hit (CRC16-CCITT-FFFF over logical 0x00-0x128 of sav-01 = 0x6494, the tail-block-63 byte pattern) is rejected as spurious: meaningless range end, no reproduction on sav-00, within chance expectation. No checksum routine exists among recovered save functions. Integrity appears to rest on the 16-byte magic alone.

checksums.name: candidate_trailer_value_logical_0x140
checksums.formula_detail: Unexplained u16_le 0x03F7 (1015) at logical offset 0x140 (raw stored bytes 03 F7 at raw 0x146-0x147, inside EEPROM block 40), immediately following walking-bit trailer bytes. Failed all standard checksum tests above; may be a count, packed bitfield continuation, or a non-standard integrity value whose routine was not recovered. Do not treat as a confirmed checksum.

io_driver_functions.notes: DMA3 transfer primitive (src,dst,count): programs DMA3 SAD/DAD/CNT via literal-pool pointer cells, count|0x80000000 enable, polls CNT control halfword bit 0x8000, updates WAITCNT EEPROM timing from config+6. Used by the reader in BOTH directions (command clock-out to 0x0D000000 and data clock-in), so it is the bidirectional hardware layer; classified 'read' because its only recovered use is the read path. CONFIRMED_STATIC, role in reader CONFIRMED_VERIFIED.

EEPROM read-one-block(block_address, dest): bounds-checks block < *(u16*)(config+4), builds serial start/read/address bitstream (address width = *(byte*)(config+8)), DMAs address_bits+3 halfwords to 0x0D000000 then 0x44 halfwords back, unpacks 64 bits MSB-first into 4 u16 stored reverse-order at dest+6,+4,+2,+0 (cause of raw .sav per-block byte reversal). No caller recoverable in callgraph.json or by textual FUN_/func_0x search; game-level caller and any write counterpart are absent from the 387-function corpus. CONFIRMED_VERIFIED.

caller_chains.trigger_context: EEPROM 8-byte block read. External game-level entry caller NOT PRESENT in corpus: callgraph.json gives callers:[] and textual search finds the address only at its own definition. Trigger in time: a save write burst runs frames 1317-1351 per state metadata; read presumably runs at boot/title, unproven.
caller_chains.how_mapped: Three routes: (1) ghidra/callgraph.json (387 nodes/328 edges): FUN_0809b6fc callers=[], callees=[0x0809b67c]; FUN_0809b67c callers=[0x0809b6fc]. (2) Rebuilt textual edges from every FUN_080xxxxxx(/func_0x080xxxxxx( occurrence in ghidra/decompiled.c (catches func_0x-style edges the JSON misses): '0809b6fc' occurs only at its definition; '0xd000000' occurs exactly twice, both inside it. (3) Pattern search for a second DMA3 driver (count|0x80000000 store, &0x8000 poll, 64-block stride-8 loop, magic compare): no surviving candidate. Because no caller exists, no per-caller RAM-struct mutation can be honestly listed; the reader itself writes exactly dest..dest+7 from one EEPROM block.

fields.name: header_magic_disney_snowboard

fields.evidence: Per-8-byte-block reversal of raw bytes yields ASCII DISNEY SNOWBOARD in both saves (Python: logical magic ok True/True); transform predicted by FUN_0809b6fc decompilation in ghidra/save_related_functions.c.

open_questions: Where is the EEPROM write function? Absent from the 387 decompiled functions by callgraph, textual-reference, and DMA-pattern searches; candidate location is the un-decompiled gap 0x0809b7ac-0x0809b920 or an indirect-only call path. Runtime DMA3 logging during a save (fuzzing F11) would identify it and the RAM mirror base in one run.
What is the RAM mirror address (0x02xxxxxx/0x03xxxxxx) of the save struct? The sole reader FUN_0809b6fc takes a caller-supplied dest pointer and no call site was recovered.
Who calls FUN_0809b6fc (boot/title load path, trigger context), and does the game compare the DISNEY SNOWBOARD magic there? No caller or string-compare routine exists in the corpus.

Does any integrity check exist beyond the magic? Candidate u16 0x03F7 at logical 0x140 failed sum8/sum16/xor8/xor16/CRC16(MODBUS/ARC/CCITT)/CRC32 over all plausible ranges in both views; is it a count, bitfield continuation, or a custom check whose routine was not recovered?

What do Record 0/Record 1's 30 u16_le values measure (scores/counts/times per index), and what are the 15-byte (or 5-byte) table entries, the walking-bit trailer, and tail blocks 61-63 semantically? Only one complete snapshot exists; fuzzing F3/F4/F6-F9 is designed to answer this.

What are the unresolved EEPROM config literal values (block limit at config+4, WAITCNT bits at +6, address width at +8) and the DMA3 register cells behind _DAT_0809b6dc.._DAT_0809b6f8? Roles are proven by access pattern; literal values are not in the corpus.
Are FUN_0809b510 (switch on 4/0x40) and FUN_0809b578 (range 0..3) related SDK mode setters for the save/media subsystem? Neither references 0x0D000000 or DMA3, so no save role is claimed.

Does normal gameplay rewrite the whole 512-byte image or only dirty blocks? Two snapshots of a single burst (frames 1317-1351) show full-layout completion but cannot distinguish full-image flush from sequential first-time formatting.
